Expectancy is 0.6bp against a 5bp assumed cost: the edge is ~8x SMALLER than the cost, and 2x-cost stress is "no" for every one of the 7 classes. audit2's own POD-EQUITY-BREAKOUT has ZERO forward rows, so the sleeve you would fund at $400 cannot be tested yet. My position: keep the rotation sleeve PAPER until it clears your own graduation gate (n>=200 forward) - 90/0/10 today, 70/20/10 only after the arm accrues.

(b) A random-entry control is NOT sufficient on its own. It tests entry timing; it does not test selection or beta exposure. A sector-rotation sleeve can beat random entries purely by holding high-beta sectors in a rising tape. You need a SECOND arm: beta-matched same-universe buy-and-hold (equal-weight sector basket held over the identical entry-to-exit windows). That is exactly the selection-alpha (G8) test, and in audit3 selection_alpha.available=false right now, so G8 cannot run at all - which is why 0 CANDIDATE is structurally forced, not statistically earned.

(c) I am not claiming a sleeve. If one is assigned, give me ETF rotation, because the exit rule dominates: rr_ratio across 3497 closed rows is median 1.67 (p10 1.50, p90 1.69) = a near-fixed 1.67:1 template, breakeven WR 37.5%. CRYPTO realises 40.42% and STILL nets -0.3089%/trade after 0.0996% slippage. So the first A/B on any sleeve is TP/SL and exit style, not signal.
